project.objective: Did Katalin Horák and her husband István Banyári of Kľak, Nová Baňa, Slovakia have a son named János, baptized 1 September 1844?

questions.question: Does the baptismal register for the Kľak (Klak) parish, Bars County, Kingdom of Hungary, contain an entry recording the baptism of János Banyári, son of István Banyári and Katalin Horák, on 1 September 1844?
questions.rationale: The objective asks whether a specific baptism occurred. The answer lies in surviving Catholic (or other church) baptismal registers for the Kľak parish, ca. 1844. This is a single testable fact — presence or absence of the entry — and the primary record type is the parish register, which FamilySearch has microfilmed for many Slovak/Hungarian localities. No prior questions need to be resolved before this one can be pursued.

log.notes: 30 results returned but all are phonetic neighbours (Kajári, Bajári, Bagyári, Fojári) — none are Banyári or a recognisable variant. All scores identical (2.807), events arrays empty. No confident match. Retrying with unaccented surname and without parent filters.

Unaccented surname variant. Top result is Kajari Janos baptised 1844 in Szeged, Csongrád — wrong county entirely. All other results lack date/place data. No Banyári/Banyari entries visible. Retrying with parent-name pivot: search the father István Banyári as principal to see if child entries exist under his name.

Father-pivot search: top 2 'Banyari Istvan' entries read via record_read — both from Mohol, Bács-Bodrog county (1892 and 1894), mother Julianna Toth. Wrong county, wrong family entirely. Collection 1743180 does not appear to hold indexed entries for the Banyári family of Klak, Bars County. Advancing to pli_002 (Hungary Baptisms 1734-1895, collection 1804226).
Zero results. Collection 1804226 (Hungary Baptisms 1734-1895) contains no indexed entry for János Banyári 1843-1845 with these parents.
Broadened to unaccented surname, no year or parent filters. Still zero results. Collection 1804226 does not index Banyári/Banyari baptisms for the Klak/Bars County area.

Top result (score 7.11, far above all others): János Banyári, baptism 01 Sep 1844, Kľak, Nová Baňa, Slovakia — exact place and date match. Father: István Banyári (confirmed). HOWEVER, mother is indexed as Káti Liskovics — NOT Katalin Horák as the research objective assumes. Káti is a diminutive of Katalin but Liskovics and Horák are different surnames. This is a material discrepancy requiring resolution. Record: ark:/61903/1:1:KDVC-BPB. Additional family member records also returned (pli_003 rank 2–3: Joannes Banyári as father of Catharina and Anna Banyári — likely the same man at a later date). Passing primary record to extraction.
Zero results. Exact bride+groom names with diacritics in Slovakia Church Books, marriage 1815-1843. No parents marriage record indexed for this couple.
Zero results. Exact groom+bride names in Hungary Catholic Church Records, marriage 1815-1843. No parents marriage record indexed here either.

Dropped spouse filter; searched Katalin Horák alone in collection 1554443, marriage 1815-1843. 38 results returned — all brides marrying men with other surnames (Kadlecz, Boskovits, Kozicz, Višnovský, Hargaš, etc.). No Banyári groom appears in any result. Top ranked match score 0.056 against LDSJ-SXL (no dated facts on subject so ranking is weak). Negative finding for the parents marriage.

Searched István Banyári marriage alone in collection 1554443, 1815-1843. Only 2 results — both for 'Steph Bajori' born 1785, a different person and era. LDSJ-SX2 has no dated facts so ranking was withheld. Negative.

Tested alternative hypothesis: searched Katalin Liskovics (the mother surname from the baptism index) for a marriage in collection 1554443, 1815-1843. 129 results with phonetic '-kovics' variants (Blaskovits, Broskovics, Greskovics, Riskovics, Florkovics, etc.) — none named Liskovics marrying a Banyári. The Liskovics marriage is equally unindexed. This neither confirms nor refutes the Liskovics hypothesis. Negative for indexed evidence.

conflicts.description: The Slovakia Church and Synagogue Books index (src_001) names the mother of János Banyári as 'Káti Liskovics'. The research question and tree name the mother as 'Katalin Horák' (LDSJ-SXL). 'Káti' is the standard Hungarian diminutive of 'Katalin' — given name consistent. 'Liskovics' vs. 'Horák' are entirely different surnames. Two explanations: (1) volunteer indexer transcription error from the original Gothic-script Catholic register; (2) the mother is genuinely Katalin Liskovics, a different woman, meaning LDSJ-SXL is misidentified in the tree as István Banyári's wife. Original-image examination (ark:/61903/3:1:33SQ-GTMD-9MWZ) is decisive but was blocked by missing OpenRouter API key. A parents' marriage record search (pli_005) may independently confirm or refute the Horák identification.
conflicts.identity_question: Is the 'Káti Liskovics' named as mother in the 01 Sep 1844 Kľak baptism record (ark:/61903/1:1:KDVC-BPB) the same person as Katalin Horák (LDSJ-SXL) in the tree?
conflicts.independence_analysis: The conflict rests on a single derivative source (src_001, the FamilySearch volunteer index of the Slovakia Church Books). No independent original-source assertion for the mother's surname has been recovered. With only one source family, no independence analysis is possible — there is nothing to weigh against a_009 except the research premise.
conflicts.weighing_analysis: a_009 ('Káti Liskovics') comes from a derivative indexed source, which carries an inherent risk of transcription error from the original Gothic-script Catholic register. The counter-proposition (mother is Katalin Horák, LDSJ-SXL) derives from the research premise and tree, unsupported by any extracted original-source assertion. No original-image assertion exists. The derivative source cannot be given full weight against the research premise when original-image verification was attempted but blocked. Equally, the research premise cannot override the indexed value without original-source confirmation. The weighing is therefore inconclusive: neither value can be preferred on available evidence alone.
conflicts.resolution_rationale: Conflict closed for the purpose of this research run as analytically inconclusive. The original register image (ark:/61903/3:1:33SQ-GTMD-9MWZ) is the required arbiter. Its examination was attempted but blocked by a missing OpenRouter API key (a resource constraint). The uncertainty is fully reflected in the proof summary ps_001, which is tiered 'possible' precisely because of this conflict. A future run with image-reading capability should treat this conflict as immediately re-opened and examine the image before any conclusion upgrade.

proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## János Banyári — Baptism at Kl'ak, 1 September 1844

### Conclusion

A son named **János Banyári** was baptized on **1 September 1844** at **Kl'ak, Bars County** (present-day Kl'ak, Žarnovica, Slovakia), with **István Banyári** named as father. This is directly supported by an entry in the Slovakia, Church and Synagogue Books, 1592–1935 (FamilySearch ark:/61903/1:1:KDVC-BPB). The overall conclusion is tiered **possible** because while the child's baptism is directly proved, the question's specific attribution to *Katalin Horák* as mother cannot be established from the current evidence: the baptism index names the mother as 'Káti Liskovics,' a conflict (c_001) that remains unresolved.

### Evidence

**Direct evidence (primary information) — child's baptism (a_001–a_003):** The Slovakia Church and Synagogue Books entry directly records János Banyári's name, sex, and christening date/place. These facts answer whether a son named János was baptized at Kl'ak on 01 Sep 1844 without inference.

**Indirect evidence — father identity (a_004, a_006–a_007; pe_006–pe_009):** The entry names István Banyári as father, inferred from the father column. This was linked to tree person LDSJ-SX2 at probable confidence: name matches (diacritic variant only), same village, same family. Three other tree persons named István Banyári were eliminated by hypothesis analysis (hyp_001–hyp_003).

**Unresolved conflict — mother's name (c_001; a_009):** The baptism index names the mother as **Káti Liskovics** (a_009). The research question presupposes **Katalin Horák** (LDSJ-SXL). 'Káti' is the standard Hungarian diminutive of 'Katalin' (given name consistent), but 'Liskovics' ≠ 'Horák'. Two interpretations: (1) volunteer-indexer transcription error from the Gothic-script register; (2) the mother is genuinely Katalin Liskovics. The original register image (ark:/61903/3:1:33SQ-GTMD-9MWZ) would resolve this but was blocked by a missing OpenRouter key.

### Next Step

Configure an OpenRouter API key and read the original parish image via the image-reader skill. If it confirms 'Horák', upgrade the proof tier to 'probable' or 'proved'. If it confirms 'Liskovics', tree correction is required and the question as stated cannot be proved.

localities.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Kľak (Klak), Bars County, Kingdom of Hungary (1844)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Historical name:** Klak, Bars County, Kingdom of Hungary
- **Modern name:** Kľak, Žarnovica District, Slovakia
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Bars County, Kingdom of Hungary → Austro-Hungarian Empire
- **Economy:** Agriculture; nearby Nová Baňa was a historic gold/silver mining town
- **Ethnic composition:** Predominantly Slovak-speaking; Hungarian-administered county
- **Religious denominations:** Roman Catholic (dominant); minority Lutheran presence possible
- **Key note:** Hungarian civil registration began 1 October 1895 — all 1844 vital events recorded exclusively by the church

## Primary record set
- **Cirkevná matrika, 1758–1896** — FamilySearch Catalog #1162429; held by Štátny okresný archív v Banskej Bystrici; **browse-only images** (no name index); covers 1844 ✓
- Browse via collection 1554443 (Slovakia Church & Synagogue Books): Roman Catholic → Bars → Klak → Krsty

## Indexed collections to search first
- Hungary, Catholic Church Records, 1636–1895 (FS collection 1743180) — indexed, complete
- Hungary Baptisms, 1734–1895 (FS collection 1804226) — indexed
- Hungary, Church Books, 1624–1950 (FS collection 4133831) — indexed & images

## Research tips
- Search indexed collections first; if no hit, browse catalog 1162429 page by page
- Language: Latin (possibly Hungarian post-1827)
- Search both Klak (Hungarian) and Kľak (Slovak) spellings
- Surname variants: Banyári/Banyari/Banjari; Horák/Horak
- Fallback parishes: Vyhne, Horné Hámry, Tekovská Breznica (all in Nová Baňa area)
